colour.status: Source PDF display colour; not a physical paint colour specification

frame.origin: outer paint edge of row 0 at the row start
frame.x: along the painted row (transverse to travel for control lines, along travel for centre lines)
frame.y: perpendicular to the row within the road plane; row 0 sits at y = 0, further rows at +y

measurement_endpoints: paint edge on one side of a row
opposite paint edge of the same row
measurement_evidence.method: Visual transcription of printed dimension label; not PDF pixel measurement

warnings: Shares J geometry with longitudinal paved-shoulder boundary; semantic role must remain separate.
Dimension leaders/context in reference PNG are not production paint.
Selected original paint paths require content review; original PNG remains authoritative.
Parameter-generated SVG is distinct from source vector extraction; sample extent is illustrative.

sample_note: Rectangles are generated from parameters_mm for a short sample; renderers should tile stroke_m along the anchor instead of using these directly.
semantic_notes: RMS2 J is a single 300 mm continuous white line used BOTH along expressways adjacent to paved shoulders AND as stop lines.
This candidate carries only the stop_line role; the paved-shoulder use is sg.markings.edge-paved-shoulder-j and is deliberately not a starter candidate.

source.description_on_sheet: This continuous white line is used along expressway adjacent to paved shoulder and also as stop lines.

stroke_m.extent_note: Extent along x is supplied by the placing anchor (control-line polyline or centreline segment); the sample rectangles are illustrative only.

verification.method: generate.py verify-sources re-opens the hash-pinned RMS PDF and measures the white fill rectangles inside bbox_pdf_points at 1:100.
